input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV (p0049) is the only renewal provision in the Agreement. It permits a seven-year extension of the 36-month Initial Period exercisable unilaterally "at the option of the Licensor," with no notice window for us and no cap on renewal pricing. A multi-year renewal we cannot exit is walk-away territory under the rule, and it fails the fallback (auto-renewal with a non-renewal window of ≤60 days and uplift ≤5%) on two material terms: renewal term length and our ability to decline. The clause also conflicts with Articles IV.II and IV.III of the same paragraph, which contemplate extension only "by mutual written" agreement of the parties, so the redline conforms the renewal sentence to the mutual-agreement mechanic already in the document and adds 12-month renewal terms, a 30-day opt-out and a CPI/3% uplift cap (fallback of 60 days and 5% offered in the comment).

proposal.summary: Replace Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option with mutual 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out and capped uplift
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a seven-year extension exercisable at the Licensor's sole option; our playbook allows renewal only by mutual written agreement, or 12-month renewals we can decline on 30 days' notice with uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. This aligns the renewal sentence with Articles IV.II and IV.III, which already require mutual written agreement; we can discuss a 60-day notice window and a 5% cap if helpful.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for successive additional periods of twelve (12) months by mutual written agreement of the parties, provided that either party may elect not to renew by written notice given at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current period, and any increase in fees for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding period and three percent (3%).
